images.title: Rectangle from a set angle
images.purpose: Show the finished rectangle ABCD whose diagonal AC splits the corner at A into 60 degrees and 30 degrees.
images.composition: One rectangle centred with wide white space; the diagonal and two angle arcs at A.
images.exact_structure: One rectangle ABCD with A bottom left, B bottom right, C top right, D top left; AB = 4 cm and BC about 6.9 cm. Diagonal AC in grey #6B7280. At A the angle between AB and AC is shaded teal #0072B2 and is 60 degrees; the angle between AC and AD is shaded amber #E69F00 and is 30 degrees. Small square marks at B and D to show right angles. Exactly 1 rectangle, 1 diagonal, 2 shaded angles.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any construction arcs or protractor drawn
images.takeaway: The set angle is drawn at A, the other end of the side.
images.description: Rectangle ABCD with AB 4 cm and diagonal AC dividing the corner at A into 60 degrees in teal and 30 degrees in amber.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at A and say which two angles meet there and that they add up to 90 degrees.

image_decisions.why: The finished rectangle with its two angles is the single picture.
